relations.name: Beyond the body
relations.sentence: Two completions that are not body parts at all, car and dog, both rise under B, admitting owned things outside the body as targets of the stroking, though each moves by half a point or less and the relation rests on very little mass.

residue.description: The word own is not a content completion of the fragment but a determiner that defers the noun, as in his own something, so its +0.5 describes a syntactic continuation rather than anything being stroked and it cannot belong to a relation about targets.

result.counterexamples: The clearest counterexample is chest at +1.8 and stomach at +0.4: if the A side were characterized as intimate or sensual self-contact being suppressed, these torso completions rising under B would contradict that directly, since bare-torso self-touch is at least as intimate as touching one's own fingers. Hair at +1.5 cuts the same way. These do not damage the relation as I have stated it, which is specifically about the hand as instrument, but they rule out the broader reading that B is avoiding self-touch, and anyone tempted to that broader reading should treat chest and hair as fatal to it. Weaker against relation 3: car and dog move only +0.5 and +0.3, close to the smallest movements in the set, so that relation could be noise rather than an admitted category.
result.notes: The whole difference is small in absolute terms: the largest single move is +2.9 points and eight of the eleven words move by less than 2. The two blocks are very unequal in length, but the instructions warn that this carries no meaning on its own, so I do not read the near-total one-sidedness of the shift as evidence of anything beyond a mild overall reweighting; what makes the A side interpretable is not that it is short but that its two members are the same kind of thing.
